subject: Acme Corp — buying process, stakeholder mapping & procurement exception request
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T15:23:00Z
Subject: Acme discovery recap — stakeholder map & procurement next steps

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call highlights:
- Primary use case: customer support triage + summary generation for enterprise customers (high volume, PII redaction)
- Decision criteria: latency under 300ms p50, SOC 2 evidence, predictable monthly pricing for 100k tokens/day
- Timeline: procurement + legal review in Dec, exec approval early Jan

Stakeholder mapping (from our notes):
- You (Sarah Nguyen) — champion / product lead
- Procurement (procurement@acme.com) — commercial terms
- Security & Legal — SOC 2 + data residency questions (they asked for SOC 2 summary)
- Economic buyer — likely CTO (TBD)

Action items / asks from Acme:
1) Can you share the procurement contact + expected timeline for commercial review?
2) Procurement will want standard MSA + any redlines; if they require SLA changes or discount >15% we will need internal approvals.
3) Security requested our SOC 2 summary and any specific data handling language — attaching SOC2 summary.

Attachments: soc2_summary.pdf (PDF)

I can put together a short mutual action plan once you confirm procurement contact and the economic buyer.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0142

--

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the following: 

- Procurement contact: procurement@acme.com (lead: Jacob Miller)
- Security contact: sec-requests@acme.com (lead: Priya Shah)
- Economic buyer: CTO (Daniel Park) — I'll intro him if/when we get to commercial review

Head of Product, Acme Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T11:45:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Acme discovery recap — procurement timeline — Approval needed: potential 20% discount & SLA change

Team — forwarding Acme thread. Procurement made it clear that they may ask for a commercial exception (discount up to ~20%) and a lower guaranteed uptime SLA (they want 99.8% rather than our standard 99.9%) to fit their procurement rules.

Details: 
- Account: Acme Corp (high strategic value, potential $250k ARR in year 1)
- Asks that may trigger exceptions: 20% discount, SLA change to 99.8% p50 latency target is acceptable to them but they want an additional 100ms p95 guarantee in the contract (this is effectively a stricter SLA for p95).
- Security asked for SOC 2 summary (attached) — they've flagged a few redlines but nothing blocking so far.

Attachments: acme_msa_redlines_v1.pdf, soc2_summary.pdf

Request: Can we get internal sign-off to proceed with a procurement exception if required? Specifically: 
- Commercial: allowance up to 20% discount (we normally cap at 15% for AE-level)
- SLA: temporary 99.8% uptime / additional p95 latency guarantee for the first 6 months (we'd prefer to add monitoring + a rollback clause if it impacts cost)

Please reply with approval, conditions, or if you'd like me to escalate to Finance/Legal directly. I need a yes/no by EOD Friday (2026-12-04) so I can keep procurement moving.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme discovery recap — procurement timeline — Approval needed

Marissa — I approve a one-time commercial exception up to 20% for Acme given strategic upside, with two conditions:
1) Discount is structured as a ramped credit tied to usage milestones (to protect ARR churn risk).
2) Legal signs off on the SLA language and rollback clause; do not commit to extended penality exposure.

I'll loop in Finance if they push beyond 20% or ask for multi-year credits. Good to proceed to Procurement with these guardrails.

-Aditya
VP Sales Operations
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T12:55:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme discovery recap — procurement timeline — Approval needed

Thumbs up from Security side for SOC 2 summary as-is. For SLA exceptions: we can accept a temporary 99.8% uptime and the additional p95 latency guarantee for 6 months provided:
- We include an explicit performance monitoring clause and sandboxed penalties (no open-ended financial exposure);
- We add a clause requiring Acme to provide representative production load tests within 30 days of go-live so we can validate the p95 commitment.

If Legal drafts the rollback and monitoring language, Security is comfortable.

-Rishi
Head of Security Engineering
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>, Jacob Miller <jacob.miller@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:12:00Z
Subject: Next steps & NIT: procurement exception framing + DocuSign

Hi Sarah / Jacob / Priya — thank you for the quick responses and for looping procurement/security. Quick update from our side after internal reviews: 

- Commercial: Redwood can approve a one-time, limited 20% discount as a procurement exception, subject to a ramped credit schedule tied to usage milestones (we will share the credit schedule in the MSA redlines).
- SLA: We can accept 99.8% uptime and the additional p95 latency commitment for the first 6 months only. This will include an explicit monitoring clause and a rollback mechanism if our metrics indicate the commitment materially increases cost or risk. Security has asked for a production load test within 30 days of go-live — happy to coordinate.
- Legal: we'll return the redlined MSA with the above language and the credit schedule. Attaching current redlines for reference.

Attachments: acme_msa_redlines_v1.pdf, soc2_summary.pdf
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd-1234
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACME-2026-RED-047

Next steps for Acme: 
1) Procurement to review redlines and confirm if the proposed exception terms are acceptable (Jacob / procurement@acme.com)
2) If acceptable, Legal to finalize and sign via DocuSign (link above)
3) Security to coordinate a short load-test window post-signature (we'll provide test plan)

Please let me know if you'd like a quick 30-min sync today to walk through the redlines. Otherwise I'll assume procurement will review and get back by end of week.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
